rationale: Ahmad is architecting AI-native hardware at Midjourney that needs to integrate deeply with generative AI models, while Charlie is building Expo as the default platform for developers—including the expanding wave of AI-enabled builders—to ship mobile and web apps at speed. Ahmad's conviction that next-gen AI interfaces require spatial computing and hand-tracking expertise pairs naturally with Charlie's focus on removing friction from the build cycle, creating a potential alignment on how AI hardware and AI-powered development tools could evolve together.
intro_message: Ahmad Abbas, meet Charlie Cheever — you're both betting on what comes next when AI and developer tools converge: Ahmad on the hardware interface side (spatial computing, hand-tracking), Charlie on the platform side (Expo as the default launchpad for AI-enabled builders).
